findings.title: Stray sed backup file committed
findings.description: `packages/core/tests/services/CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E` is a new 146-line file in the diff. It is the pre-edit copy of `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`, left behind by a macOS `sed -i -E` call. It still calls `createContextPipeline(...)` with the old one-argument signature. The file is outside the `*.test.ts` glob, so vitest won't run it, but it is dead duplicate code. `grep` for it already returns stale `createContextPipeline(` hits. The `.gitignore` has no pattern for it, so it will stay in the repo until someone deletes it. Delete it from the commit.

findings.title: Default instruction `'implementation'` is now repeated four times
findings.description: The new line `const instruction = project.instruction || 'implementation';` adds a fourth copy of the literal. The others are at lines 216, 244 and 289. The project rules say "never scatter comparison values" and "do not hard-code magic defaults". The duplication also carries a correctness risk: the resolver and `mapProjectToEnhancedContext` must agree on the default, or adoption eligibility could be decided on a different instruction than the one that selects the prompt. Define the default once (a constant in `constants.ts` or the schema module). Use it here and, ideally, at the three existing sites.

findings.title: Adoption failure intentionally bypasses the error-stub fallback
findings.description: `AdoptionError` is rethrown alongside `PermissivenessFragmentError`, which follows the no-silent-fallback rule. `ContextIntegrator.test.ts` covers both the rethrow and the unchanged stub behavior for unrelated errors. `persistInProgress` in `adoptionResolver.ts` catches a write failure and rethrows it as `AdoptionError` with `cause`, so the catch complies with the exception-handling rule.

findings.title: Required `adoptionStateWrites` option forces every caller to decide
findings.description: Making the option required and typed as a `'persist' | 'read-only'` union is a good contract. I grepped every `createContextPipeline(` caller in `src` and `tests`: `cf build` and `context_build` pass `persist`, `template_preview` passes `read-only`, and all test callers are updated. `isSelected` uses a `never` exhaustiveness check. The mcp-server imports `AdoptionStateWrites` through `@context-forge/core/node`, which re-exports `adoption/index.js`, so that import resolves.

findings.title: Test coverage of the selection rule and the persist/read-only split is thorough
findings.description: The 13 integration scenarios use real temp projects, covering greenfield, scaffold-only, brownfield, shallow clone, monorepo, resume, overrides, a missing guide profile and read-only mode. The unit tests cover the resolver's laziness (the source walk never runs when planning artifacts exist) and the failed-write path. The CLI/MCP parity test checks that both entry points produce identical prompts. The `chmod` test is gated by `skipIf` for Windows and root. The integration tests use a temporary `CONTEXT_FORGE_DATA_DIR`, so they cannot touch real user config.
